problem:
Which of the following statements are true?

- $v=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1\end{aligned}]$ is an eigenvector of $A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}]$ that corresponds to the eigenvalue $\lambda =2.$
- $v=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$ is an eigenvector of $A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 2 & 2\end{aligned}]$ that corresponds to the eigenvalue $\lambda =0.$
- If $v$ is an eigenvector of a matrix $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalue $\lambda =2,$ then $3v$ is an eigenvector of $A$ corresponding to $\lambda =6.$
